 Honourable Mr. Justice Rudra Prakash Mishra
 Oral Order

(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)
6 15-12-2023 The present criminal appeal has been filed under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 by the appellant-convict against the judgment of conviction dated 22.12.2020 and order of sentence dated 24.12.2020 rendered by learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Jehanabad in S. Tr.
No. 149 of 2019/70 of 2020, arising out of Kurtha P.S. case No. 157 of 2018, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been held guilty for the offence under Sections 498A, 326, 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life with fine of Rs. 10,000/- under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo two months rigorous imprisonment.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6) dt.15-12-2023

The appellant was further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years with fine of Rs. 10,000/- under Section 326 of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo two months rigorous imprisonment.

The appellant was also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years with fine of Rs. 5,000/- under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo one month rigorous imprisonment.
All the sentences were directed to run concurrently.
2. Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr. Ramakant Sharma assisted by Mr. Mayank Raj, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Sujit Kumar Singh, learned A.P.P. for the State.

sentences.text: Learned senior advocate for the appellant has submitted that the appeal filed by the appellant has been admitted and at present the appellant prays for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence imposed by the Trial Court.
Learned senior advocate has mainly submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, the occurrence took place on 14 th August, 2018 at 11:00 a.m.
However, the victim-injured, who is wife of the appellant-convict, has given her fardbeyan only on 18.08.2018 Patna High Court CR.
APP ( DB) No.177 of 2022(6) dt.15-12-2023 before the concerned Police Officer of Agamkuan Police Station, Patna
. It is submitted that the so-called fardbeyan, given by the injured-victim, was recorded on 18.08.2018.

Surprisingly, the same was registered as formal F.I.R.
before the Kurtha Police Station which is 60 kms away from Patna only on 27.08.2018 i.e. after a period of 10 days.
It is also pointed out by learned senior advocate from the record that in the fardbeyan, no impression of right leg of the victim was obtained.
From the post-mortem report of the dead body of the deceased, it is revealed that the injured-victim sustained burn injuries all over the body except portion of right soul and both palm.
Learned senior advocate, therefore, urged that it is surprising that why the thumb impression of the injured-victim was not obtained by the concerned police authority.

4. Learned senior advocate would further submit that in the present case, the prosecution has examined only four witnesses out of which two witnesses are mother and brother of the deceased,
one is the doctor and one is the investigating officer.
No independent witness has been examined by the prosecution.

It is also submitted that as per the case of the prosecution, the present appellant,
who is the husband of the deceased, poured kerosene oil on his wife and thereafter set her Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6) dt.15-12-2023 on fire.
It is reflected from the record that the appellant himself has brought his wife to the concerned hospital at Gaya from where she was referred to P.M.C.H. for better treatment.
However, the injured was admitted in Samford Hospital, Patna.

It is also submitted that the prosecution has not examined the doctor who had treated the injured-victim between the period 14.08.2018 to 24.08.2018, the date on which the victim succumbed to the injury sustained by her.
The medical papers were also not produced on record.

Learned senior counsel would, therefore, submit that marriage of the deceased and the appellant took place 11 years ago and as per the appellant, the informant herself, during the aforesaid period, most of the time, was at her parental house.

5. Learned senior advocate lastly contended that if the victim-injured was in a position to give her fardbeyan before the police on 18.08.2018 and if she was survived up to 24.08.2018, why the investigating agency had not called the Executive Magistrate for recording her dying declaration.

Learned counsel, therefore, urges that the present one is a case of false implication and when the co-accused (mother of the present appellant) is enlarged on bail, the appellant be released on bail during the pendency of the present appeal as the Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6)
dt.15-12-2023 appellant is in custody for approximately more than five years.

6. On the other hand, learned A.P.P. has opposed the request for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence by contending that once the injured-victim, who is the wife of the appellant herself, has given the fardbeyan before the Police while she was admitted in the hospital, the said fardbeyan is required to be considered by this Court while entertaining request for grant of bail.
It is submitted that the said fardbeyan was signed by the doctor of the concerned hospital where she was admitted.

sentences.text: Thus, when the doctor has made the endorsement and signed the fardbeyan, the doubt raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is ill founded.

Learned A.P.P. would thereafter submit that merely because there is delay in lodging the formal F.I.R. before the concerned Police Station, the benefit of the same cannot be given to the appellant-convict while entertaining his request for grant of bail.
Learned A.P.P. would, therefore, urge that the request for bail may not be entertained.
7. We have considered the submissions canvassed by learned counsel appearing for the parties and have also perused the materials placed on record as also the L.C.R.
From the record, it would emerge that the fardbeyan of the victim-injured was recorded on 18.08.2018 when she was in Samford Hospital, Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6) dt.15-12-2023 Patna at 13.30 hrs.
In the said fardbeyan, the victim-injured has made allegation against the appellant and mother of the appellant.
However, it is pertinent to note that even as per the said fardbeyan, the occurrence took place on 14.08.2018 at 11:00 a.m.
If the said fardbeyan is carefully examined, it transpires that no impression of right leg of the victim was obtained on the said fardbeyan.
Even, there is signature of the doctor on the said fardbeyan.

Now, it is pertinent to note that the said fardbeyan was recorded after a period of four days from the date on which she was admitted in the hospital and prosecution has prima facie not disclosed the reason for recording the fardbeyan after a period of four days.

The prosecution has also not produced any material from which it can be established that after a period of four days whether she was in a position to give her statement before the Police or before any authority.
Even the doctor, who has signed the said fardbeyan, has also not made any endorsement whether the injured was in physical state of mind to give a fardbeyan before the police or not.

It is also relevant to note at this stage that the injured survived up to 24.08.2018 and though the occurrence is of 14.08.2018, the investigating agency has not called the Executive Magistrate for recording the dying declaration of the victim.

Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6)
dt.15-12-2023 8.

From the post-mortem report of the deceased, it is also revealed that the doctor who had conducted post-mortem of the dead body of the deceased has observed that the deceased sustained injures all over the body except portion of right soul and both palm.
Thus, from the aforesaid, it can be said that the thumb impression of the victim can be obtained on the fardbeyan.

However,
surprisingly the impression of the right toe was obtained on the fardbeyan.

At this stage, it is also pertinent to note that it is specific case of the learned senior advocate for the appellant that the fardbeyan was recorded on 18.08.2018 at 13.30 hours in Samford Hospital, Patna.
The copy of the said fardbeyan was sent to the Kurtha Police Station only on 27.08.2018 when the formal F.I.R. was registered before the said police station on 27.08.2018.
It is specific case of the appellant that distance between the Patna and Kurtha Police Station is 60 kms.
The prosecution has also failed to explain the said delay in registering the formal F.I.R. before the concerned police station.
9. In view of the aforesaid overall facts and circumstances of the present case, we are of the view that the appellant is required to be released on bail during the pendency of the appeal.
Accordingly, the appellant is ordered to be Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.177 of 2022(6) dt.15-12-2023 released on bail during the pendency of the present appeal on executing bond of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees fifteen thousand) and upon furnishing two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Jehanabad in S. Tr. No. 149 of 2019/70 of 2020, arising out of Kurtha Rohit Sharma vs The State Of Bihar on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32004015/

11. The appellant should co-operate in this Court till disposal of this appeal.
12. The sentence shall remain suspended in the meanwhile.
Realization of the fine, if any, shall also remain stayed during pendency of this appeal.
